ranking.note: Raised to P2: same class of defect as #36105 (shipped bitcoin wrapper broken on a real platform/packaging layout), so the two must share a band.
Band unchanged; placed below the concrete IPC crash/platform fixes because its value is scaffolding for future online wallet commands rather than a present defect.
Band unchanged; single unique commit at the top of the #10102/#19460 stack, so it is the last link of the chain to need attention.
Lowered to P3: an interfaces::Node method addition serving draft GUI consumers, same consequence class as #36597, which sits at P3.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain: #36520 -> #29409 -> #10102 -> #19460 -> #19461. Review in that order; #36520 (crash hardening) and #29409 (Chain over IPC) gate the whole process-separation milestone even though #10102 carries the larger benefit.

#32387 (ipc: add windows support) states it also 'fixes the Windows wrapper executable to properly await child processes', which is exactly what #36105 does standalone. #36105 looks like the extracted piece; review it first and confirm #32387 is rebased on it to avoid duplicate/conflicting changes.

#35932 and #36572 both fix disconnect-time use-after-free in the IPC layer. #35932 is kept P1 only because it has reported crash evidence (Antithesis #35845/#33387); #36572 is the same failure mode without a filed crash. If a reviewer finds real-world occurrences for #36572 it belongs at P1 too. Review #35932 first.
#36190 only tests behaviour introduced by #36105; it is dead weight until #36105 lands, so #36105 must be reviewed first.
#33117 and #36597 solve the same shape of problem (expose node/wallet state to out-of-process GUI frontends through the interface layer) and are now banded together; neither is IPC mechanics itself.
#35932 and #36097 both carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits pending upstream (libmultiprocess#335 and #342); the subtree sync order between them should be settled before either merges.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: four P1s covering the core separation chain and IPC crash/disconnect correctness; a P2 block of platform coverage, wrapper bugs and mining-interface enablement; and a P3 tail of tests, build checks, and interface additions whose consumers are themselves drafts. Only two band moves were needed (#36106 up, #33117 down), both for parity with a near-identical PR already on the list.
